title: Operational SLO Orchestration Crosswalk — Notebook
content:
Purpose
This is a working notebook for the operational SLO orchestration crosswalk — a compact, execution-focused reference for the cross-functional team (SRE, platform, product, serving runtime, and solutions). The aim: converge on a repeatable sprint pattern for moving service-level objectives from design → test → rollout → monitoring → incident play integration.

Context and why this doc exists (notes to self)
- We have multiple stalled SLO efforts: some teams ship SLOs but never wire into oncall flows; others define SLOs that are impossible to measure in the current pipeline.
- Need a pragmatic, small-batch execution pattern that forces decisions early (measurement, owner, rollback criteria).
- This doc collects tactical steps, a sprint-by-sprint experiment plan, and a running decision log. Treat as living; prefer bullets and ACTION items.

High-level goals (what success looks like)
- By end of quarter, 6 product services have operational SLOs with: a) automated measurement in metrics pipeline, b) SLO alerting linked to runbooks, c) a documented rollback/fallback policy.
- Reduce 95th-pct latency regressions going to customers by 30% for SLO-covered routes.
- Decrease time-to-oncall-onboarding for new SLOs to < 3 days (from creating SLO to alerting + runbook).

Scope (what this notebook covers)
- Service selection criteria, measurement decisions, required infra changes, owner assignments, sprint tasks, stakeholder approvals, communication cadence, and the decision log.
- Out of scope: full governance sign-off process for enterprise Private customers (that follows separate compliance flow).

Stakeholders and roles (proposed)
- SRE (Lead): Priya Patel — orchestration, final sign-off for rollout readiness
- Platform/Infra: Luca Moretti — metrics pipeline, exporter changes, ingestion latency checks
- Product/Feature PM: Aisha Ramirez — acceptance criteria, user-impact tradeoffs, customer comms when applicable
- Serving Runtime: Maya Chen — performance constraints, batching interactions, model variant fallbacks
- Solutions/SE: Tom O'Neill — customer-facing runbook template and demo collateral
- Oncall SME pool: rotations from eng teams (TBD)

Minimum gating checklist for an "operational SLO" (must be YES to proceed to rollout)
- Measurement: Metric exists and is stable in prod metrics (no major label cardinality explosion).
- Alerting: SLI->SLO->Alert mapped and actionable (1 P1 alert for burn-rate; 1 P2 for long-term drift).
- Runbook: At least one short, step-by-step remediation and rollback action documented in the runbook.
- Ownership: Primary owner assigned and shadow oncall linked.
- Fallout plan: Fallback behavior (throttling to lower-cost model, regional failover, or degrade gracefully) defined.
- Capacity check: Dedicated/hosted routing policies evaluated to avoid capacity starvation.

Execution pattern (90-day experiment composed of 3 sprints)
Sprint 0 (2 weeks) — Discovery & minimal instrumenting
- Select 3 pilot services using selection heuristic: high-customer-impact endpoints + medium traffic + manageable complexity. (ACTION: product to nominate by 2026-09-20).
- For each pilot: define the candidate SLO (objective, time-window, target), primary SLI expression, and measurement query (PromQL or statsd tag).
- Platform: run quick experiment to ensure metric cardinality under threshold; ticket infra work if > x labels.
- Decision: keep or discard based on measurement feasibility.

Sprint 1 (3 weeks) — Implement measurement + alert prototypes
- Implement exporter/metric change PRs for each pilot. (Owner: platform)
- End-to-end validation: simulate synthetic traffic to validate measurement correctness and latency of metric ingestion (< 10s if possible).
- Create initial alert rules: one burn-rate alert for short window and one drift alert for long window.
- Draft runbook templates attached to each alert.
- Quick tabletop with oncall: run through the alert, validate runbook effectiveness.

Sprint 2 (3 weeks) — Canary rollout + monitor + refine
- Canary SLO enablement: route 5–10% of traffic through SLO path or enable alerting in staging flagged to oncall test harness.
- Monitor false positives and tune thresholds. Document every change in the decision log.
- Post-canary retro and decision: promote to full rollout if false-positive rate < 5% and remediation steps work.

Operational details and engineering notes (practical constraints)
- Canonical SLI storage: metrics-agg namespace in Prometheus/Thanos. Prefer histograms for latency SLIs with agreed bucketing.
- Labeling standard: service=, route=, model_variant=, region= — minimal set to avoid explosion.
- Aggregation windows: use sliding 5m for burn-rate; 28d for availability baseline. Document reasoning per SLO.
- Cost note: increased label cardinality or high-resolution histograms may increase metrics cost; capture cost estimate in the infra ticket.

Communication & approval cadence
- Weekly triage sync (30m): Mon 10:00 — demo measurement + blockers. Invite: SRE lead, platform lead, PM lead, runtime lead.
- Triage channel: #slo-orchestration (public channel) and #slo-private-escalations (for sensitive customer signal).
- Stakeholder review: End of sprint demo + decision signoff doc in Confluence (linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE-1234).

Decision log (running)
- 2026-09-16: Chose pilot heuristic (impact x traffic x complexity). Rational: balances risk and value. — Priya
- 2026-09-22: Rejected SLO candidate for service X due to >2000 unique model_variant labels. Action: consider aggregated model_variant or use sampling. — Luca
- 2026-10-05: Burn-rate alert window shortened to 10m from 30m after synthetic load test exposed detection lag. — Maya

Risks, mitigations, open questions
- Risk: Alert fatigue from too many new SLO alerts. Mitigation: only ship one P1 burn-rate and one P2 drift per service initially; schedule a 2-week quiet window post-rollout.
- Risk: Metric cardinality drives cost. Mitigation: aggregated labels, selective sampling, or pre-aggregation in exporter.
- Open question: Who maintains long-term SLO dashboards? Proposal: SRE owns dashboard templates; product owns long-term target review cadence.

Example sprint tasks (checklist form)
- [ ] PM nominates pilot services (due 2026-09-20)
- [ ] Platform creates exporter PRs and deploys (owner: Luca)
- [ ] SRE wires alerts into PagerDuty with runbook link
- [ ] Runtime team verifies fallback policy feasibility and documents any required changes
- [ ] Solutions drafts customer-facing note if rollout touches customer-visible behavior
- [ ] Retrospective + promote/discard decision logged in Confluence

Acceptance criteria for "Promote to full rollout"
- Measurement validated in production for 48h with acceptable error bounds
- False positive rate < 5% in canary window
- Runbook tested in at least one oncall tabletop execution
- Primary owner and shadow oncall assigned

Next steps (near-term)
- 2026-11-03: Kickoff sprint 0. Agenda: pick pilots, confirm owner matrix, open infra tickets.
- ACTION: Priya to create Sprint 0 board (Jira epic JIRA-SRE-7890) and invite stakeholders.
- ACTION: Luca to run a metrics-cardinality script against nominated services and report back by 2026-09-24.

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments
- Could use sampling + fast-approx histogram for high-cardinality routes. Explore trade-off with accuracy.
- Consider a one-click SLO template in Console for "developer-mode" that sets up the measurement + dashboard + runbook skeleton. Long-term RD but could be an Engage feature.
- Keep decisions small. If a SLO needs infra >2 weeks, defer to next-quarter cadence unless high priority.

Appendix: Templates and links
- Runbook template: short summary, triage steps, mitigation toggles, rollback criteria, postmortem triggers
- Measurement template: SLI expression, aggregation window, test script, synthetic traffic plan

If you copy or edit this doc: keep the decision log at the top and prefix decisions with date + owner. This makes it easy to review when hunting for changes.

—— end notebook ——
